stem: A crop moves from a low-buffering substrate to one with substantially different cation-exchange behavior. How should the nutrient program be handled?
choices: Use the previous program unchanged at first because fertilizer concentration determines plant nutrition more strongly than differences in exchange behavior between media
Raise nutrient-solution EC in proportion to the medium's exchange capacity so more cations remain in solution and the previous root-zone concentration is preserved
Treat the previous recipe as a starting point and validate root-zone pH/EC, plant response, and nutrient behavior in the new medium
Reduce the micronutrient fraction during the transition because media with greater exchange capacity tend to retain trace elements more strongly than macronutrients
rationale: Media chemistry can change nutrient retention and buffering. A recipe that worked in one medium should be validated under the new root-zone conditions rather than assumed to transfer unchanged.
